quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #19
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: How can you check your blind spot when changing lanes?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Use your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Mirrors do not show all areas around your vehicle. There are blind spots you cannot see in mirrors. Always look over your shoulder before changing lanes to check these areas.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.
You should never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to vehicles coming straight toward you. You must always yield to pedestrians.

questions.question: Before driving, remove all snow, frost, and ice from:

options.text: Just the windshield.
All windows.
Just the windshield and passenger window.

questions.correctAnswerText: All windows.
questions.explanation: You need to see clearly through all your windows. Remove all snow, ice, and frost from every window and mirror before you drive.

questions.question: When a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane is crossing the street, what should you do?

options.text: You must always yield the right-of-way.
You must tell them where to cross.
You only have to yield at intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog means the pedestrian is blind or partially blind. You must always yield to these pedestrians.

questions.question: If you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane, what should you do?

options.text: The pedestrian must yield to you.
You must yield the right-of-way.
Honk your horn to alert them.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog means the pedestrian is blind or partially blind. You must always yield to these pedestrians.

questions.question: What should a driver do about the right-of-way?

options.text: Assume all drivers automatically follow right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Do not assume you have the right-of-way, even if the rules say you do. Always look at the situation. Give up your right-of-way if it helps prevent a crash.

questions.question: Only ____ can reduce blood alcohol content (BAC).

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating fatty foods
Time

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle on the left, when is it safe to move back to the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You can move back into the right lane when you see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: Which statement about driving speed is true?

options.text: As speed increases, the chance of death in a crash increases.
As speed increases, you should increase your following distance.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds make crashes more deadly. Faster speeds need longer stopping distances, so increase your following distance when you drive faster.

questions.question: If you are following a school bus or tank truck, what should you do?

options.text: Pass them on the right.
Be prepared to stop at all railroad crossings.
Expect them to drive above the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared to stop at all railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: School buses and tank trucks must stop at all railroad crossings. Be ready to stop if you are following one of these vehicles.

questions.question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change with vehicle speed?

options.text: They decrease as speed increases.
They are not affected by speed.
They increase as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds mean longer stopping distances and more severe crashes.

questions.question: When you see this yellow sign, you should:

options.text: Always stop at the crosswalk.
Stop and wait for a crossing guard to signal you.
Be ready to stop if children are in the crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if children are in the crosswalk.
questions.explanation: A five-sided sign means you are near a school. Stay alert and stop if you see children in the crosswalk.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines between traffic lanes mean?

options.text: You can pass from the left.
You can pass from the right.
You cannot pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed from either side.

questions.question: When a school bus has red flashing lights, you must stay stopped until:

options.text: All students get off the bus.
The stop arm goes back in.
The stop arm goes back in and the bus starts moving.

questions.correctAnswerText: The stop arm goes back in and the bus starts moving.
questions.explanation: You must stay stopped until the red lights turn off, the stop arm is pulled in, and the bus moves again.

questions.question: You are in an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches with its siren and flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop right away in the intersection.
Pull to the right of the intersection and stop.
Drive through the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive through the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: If you are in an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches, finish crossing. Then drive to the right and stop. Always give the right-of-way to police cars, fire trucks, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights.

questions.question: If your vehicle breaks down, what should you do?

options.text: Signal and move to the slow lane.
Stop in your lane and turn on hazard lights.
Turn on hazard lights and drive off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on hazard lights and drive off the road.
questions.explanation: Get your vehicle off the road and away from traffic if you can. Turn on your emergency flashers so other drivers know you are in trouble.

questions.question: What color are traffic control devices in construction and work zones?

options.text: Red.
Orange.
Yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange.
questions.explanation: Orange signs, cones, and barriers are used in work zones. Drive with extra care when you see orange warning devices on the road.

questions.question: Fatigue increases the risk of:

options.text: Missing an exit.
Being late for an appointment.
Falling asleep while driving and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep while driving and crashing.
questions.explanation: Fatigue slows your decision-making and increases crash risk. When tired, you could fall asleep at the wheel and hurt or kill yourself or others.

questions.question: In a motor vehicle on a highway, what is legal regarding alcohol?

options.text: It is illegal to drink from or carry open alcohol containers.
Passengers can drink alcohol.
Drivers can drink if they are not drunk.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is illegal to drink from or carry open alcohol containers.
questions.explanation: You cannot drive under the influence of alcohol. Neither drivers nor passengers can have open alcohol containers in a running vehicle.

questions.question: On a freeway, why should you look farther ahead than on a city street?

options.text: To spot hazards early.
Because stopping takes a quarter mile.
To keep up with traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: To spot hazards early.
questions.explanation: On the freeway, watch for traffic changes ahead. Look for signals from other drivers. Be ready for merging vehicles at on-ramps and prepare for rapid changes in road conditions.

questions.question: What does this yellow sign mean?

options.text: There is a sharp turn to the right.
The lane must turn right.
A right turn is permitted on a green arrow only.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a sharp turn to the right.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow-green. They warn drivers about upcoming road conditions like curves and sharp turns.

questions.question: What does this black and yellow sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is for one-way traffic only.
There is a detour to the right due to road construction.
The road ahead changes direction at an extreme angle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead changes direction at an extreme angle.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions ahead. This sign tells drivers to slow down for a sharp change in road direction.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection?

options.text: Come to a complete stop at the intersection.
Maintain your normal speed.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should be alert. Slow down and be careful as you proceed through the intersection.

questions.question: What must you do when a school bus ahead on your side of the road has its red lights flashing?

options.text: Slow to a speed no faster than 10 mph.
Stop until the lights stop flashing.
Change lanes and pass cautiously.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the lights stop flashing.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights and a stop arm, it is loading or unloading students. You must stop and wait until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled back. Never pass a stopped school bus.

questions.question: What should you do when driving near a large commercial vehicle?

options.text: Follow the large vehicle closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.
Avoid driving beside it for long stretches of time.
Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving beside it for long stretches of time.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have large blind spots on each side. Do not drive beside them for long periods of time.

questions.question: How do you know where traffic is behind you?

options.text: Frequently check your rearview mirror.
Turn and look out your back window.
Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Frequently check your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror often to see traffic behind you.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Steep grade ahead.
The road ahead winds with a series of turns or curves.
Slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that the road will be slippery when wet. Drive carefully in wet conditions.

questions.question: If a child is about to run into the street, what should you do?

options.text: Start to prepare to slow down.
Flash your headlights.
Sound a sharp blast of your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sound a sharp blast of your horn.
questions.explanation: If a child or pedestrian is about to enter the street in front of you, sound a sharp blast on your horn to warn them.

questions.question: A vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you. What should you do first?

options.text: Honk and step on the brake firmly.
Take your foot off the gas pedal.
Swerve into the lane next to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a vehicle cuts in front of you, release the accelerator. This creates space without requiring you to brake hard or swerve.

questions.question: What do yellow lines separate?

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of two-way roads. A solid yellow line means you cannot cross to pass. A broken yellow line means you can cross to pass if it is safe.

questions.question: After a train passes at a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Wait for the signal lights to stop flashing.
Watch for a second train.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: After a train passes, watch for a second train on any track. Do not drive until all gates are up and all warning lights stop flashing.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in work zones?

options.text: Follow the car in front of you closely.
Pass the car in front of you as soon as you can.
Keep a safe distance and do not tailgate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a safe distance and do not tailgate.
questions.explanation: In work zones, keep space between your car and barriers, trucks, equipment, workers, and other cars. Increase your following distance and never tailgate.

questions.question: A blood alcohol level of 0.02 percent:

options.text: Will not affect your driving.
Will not put other drivers at risk.
Will double your chances of having an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will double your chances of having an accident.
questions.explanation: Each 0.02 percent increase in blood alcohol level nearly doubles your risk of a fatal crash.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, what is the minimum following distance you should maintain?

options.text: One second.
Two seconds.
Three seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds.
questions.explanation: More distance between cars gives you more time to react. Keep at least three seconds between your car and others in normal conditions. Increase this distance in bad weather or heavy traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn left.
No left turn allowed.
No U-turn allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn allowed.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers they cannot turn left. It is unsafe and illegal to turn left where this sign is posted.

questions.question: Where should your hands be on the steering wheel to turn quickly?

options.text: On opposite sides of the wheel.
Next to each other at the top of the wheel.
One at the top and one at the bottom of the wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: On opposite sides of the wheel.
questions.explanation: Place both hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel. This position is comfortable and helps you turn safely on highways.

questions.question: Your reaction time becomes slower after:

options.text: Drinking alcohol.
Sleeping.
Working hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drinking alcohol.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes, reduces your vision, and makes you less alert. It also impairs your judgment and driving skills. You will have trouble judging distance, speed, and where other vehicles are.

questions.question: How can you avoid skidding on slippery surfaces?

options.text: Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.
Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.
Slow down before entering curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve because you cannot see what is ahead. Braking while turning can cause you to skid.

questions.question: If you see animals near the roadway while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to scare them away.
Slow down and drive with caution.
Quickly swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and drive with caution.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful if you see animals near the road. They may suddenly move or change direction. Some animals travel in groups, so there may be more animals out of sight.

questions.question: When should you check your rearview mirrors?

options.text: Often to see traffic moving behind you.
To check if a vehicle is in your blind spot.
Only when you are slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often to see traffic moving behind you.
questions.explanation: While driving, do not look at one thing for too long. Check your rearview mirrors often so you know where nearby vehicles are.
